entries.en: Commander Shepard, my name is Nassana Dantius. I have a job for you. I can't say any more in an unsecured communication.
If you're interested in hearing my offer, meet me on the Citadel so we can talk in person. I'll be waiting in the diplomat's lounge on the Presidium.
Commander Shepard, I am Nassana Dantius.
I am glad you are here. I must talk to you about my sister, Dahlia. She has been kidnapped by slavers!
I see you got my message.
I do. My sister Dahlia is a crewman on a cargo vessel operating out beyond the fringes of the Traverse. Her ship was attacked by privateers. There were no reported survivors.
This is where it gets complicated. Last week, I received a message with her voice on it. Dahlia is alive!
The rest of the crew was killed, but she was taken prisoner. The slavers demanded a huge ransom from me in exchange for returning her unharmed.
My sister probably told them who she was. My family is very wealthy, Shepard. They must have realized she was worth more to them alive.
That's what I thought. I did what they wanted, transferred the funds to the account they specified. Only, they never released her. They haven't contacted me since.
I've already transferred the funds to the account they specified. Only, they never released her. They haven't contacted me since.
It's too late. I transferred the funds to the account they specified. Only, they never released her. They haven't contacted me since.
I've made a terrible mistake, Shepard. I am a diplomatic emissary! By law, I am required to report any attempted extortion to C-Sec immediately.
But I was afraid for Dahlia, so I just paid the ransom. Now she is still missing, and if anyone finds out what I did I could end up in jail!
Government representatives on the Citadel are not allowed to negotiate with terrorists. It is too dangerous. Paying a ransom would only encourage more kidnappings.
I support the law in theory, but when I got the message, all I could think about was Dahlia's safety.
I doubt they would actually send me to prison for what I did. But they would strip me of my post, and Dahlia would still be in the hands of the slavers.
You only need to bring her back. I have already found her for you.
This is easy money for you, Shepard. I have already found her; you just need to bring her back.
Yes, Shepard? Did you find my sister?
I know you. You're Commander Shepard. The human Spectre.
Dahlia's dead, Nassana. And I know she was blackmailing you.
I killed Dahlia myself. And I know she was blackmailing you.
It sounded like you needed some help.
You said you had a job offer.
I'm sorry for your loss.
You want me to hunt down the people who killed her.
Why didn't the raiders kill Dahlia along with everyone else?
Coming up with the ransom seems like the best way to ensure Dahlia's safety.
Do you want me to deliver the ransom?
You can't negotiate with criminals.
Why would they put you in jail? You're the victim here!
You want me to find her and bring her back.
You got in over your head and you expect me to pull you out?
Dahlia's dead. And I know she was blackmailing you.
Dahlia's dead. I killed her myself. If you don't want to end up like her, start talking!
I know the truth.
Don't lie to me.
Actually, she's dead.
Are you in trouble?
Get to the point.
What do you want?
That's too bad.
Now you want revenge.
I know what this is about.
Why was your sister spared?
You'd better pay.
What's my part?
Don't pay the ransom!
That's a stupid law!
You need my help.
So you came to me.
So I have to fix your mess?
So you came to me.
I found her.
You lied to me!
Hm. And I was all set to try to manipulate you into hunting her down for me. But I guess that won't be necessary now, will it?
I tracked the ransom payment through several accounts. Eventually, it lead to a small mercenary band operating out of the Artemis Tau cluster.
I need you to go to the merc base, take them out, and bring my sister back. You shall be well rewarded.
Thank you, Shepard. I knew you were the right man for the job.
Thank you, Shepard. I knew you were the right woman for the job.
Come back and see me when the job is done.
You are the only one I can turn to, Shepard! Besides, I have already transmitted the coordinates to your ship.
Please, just see what you can do. I will be waiting here when you're done.
So the truth comes out. I hope you are not angry. Surely you can understand why I lied to you?
No need to raise your voice, Commander. Surely you can understand why I lied to you?
If people found out my sister was a criminal, I'd be considered a security risk. They'd revoke my clearance, or place me on administrative leave until she was apprehended.
That is why I misled you. I could not risk you exposing me. But now that Dahlia is out of the picture, it is no longer a problem.
Perhaps you are right. I am sorry. We have trust issues in my family.
I am sorry I wasn't honest with you. We have trust issues in my family.
I could not agree more. She was my sister, but I will not shed any tears for her death.
I shall transfer a little something into your account as a token of my appreciation. I'm sure you will find the amount satisfactory.
You make a good point. Anyone can come up with credits. But I can give you authorization to purchase prototype asari mods.
True, but I am the only one who can authorize you to purchase prototype asari mods.
I will get you added to our manufacturer's preferred client list. I think you would be very interested in what they have available.
Goodbye, Shepard. It has been a pleasure doing business with you.
I do not like being in anyone's debt. Consider it a fee for doing your civic duty if it makes you feel any better.
Or give it away to some charity. I care not. The funds are already on their way. They are your problem now.
Understood, Shepard. I will not bother you again.
I am not that stupid. You will get a fair deal. A very fair deal.
Goodbye, Shepard.
I do not want to take chances with my sister's life. I need a Spectre.
Besides, you operate outside official channels. My superiors cannot find out I never reported the ransom in the first place.
I have resources. Contacts and credits can go a long way, especially if you are willing to bend the rules.
I already broke the law when I paid the ransom. This couldn't make things any worse.
Pretty much what you'd expect: rough, dangerous, and well-armed. Nothing a Spectre cannot handle, though.
Come back and see me when the job is done.
Is there something I can do for you?
What? Are you saying she's...
I gave you what you wanted, Shepard. We have nothing more to discuss.
Thank you for all your help, Shepard.
I don't have time to talk now. I'm very busy.
Keep your reward. I'll bring your sister back. I promise.
Don't worry. I'll bring your sister back.
I've got more important things to do than track down your sister.
I would've helped if you'd just told me the truth.
Do your own dirty work next time!
Your sister was a slaver. She got what was coming to her.
You're a diplomat on her way up the ranks. It could be handy to have a Spectre who owes you a favor.
I'm a Spectre, not some merc for hire. I can find credits anywhere.
I don't want your blood money.
I just want to put this whole thing behind me.
If you try to cheat me on this--
Can't you hire someone else to do this?
How'd you find out who was behind the ransom?
Anything you can tell me about the mercs who have your sister?
I have to go.
You're Nassana, right? I ran into your sister, Dahlia. It didn't end well for her.
Never mind.
I don't do this for payment.
I'll do it.
Forget it.
Why me?
Tracking the ransom.
Kidnappers
Goodbye.
You should have told me.
I don't like being used.
She deserved to die.
I've got a better deal.
Credits won't cut it.
Don't bother.
Fair enough.
It better be.
I ran into your sister.
Goodbye.
I know the truth.
She is.
I killed her myself.
You wanted your sister dead?
Wait... You wanted your sister dead?
You wanted your sister dead?
You wanted your sister dead?
You wanted your sister dead?
You wanted your sister dead?
Obviously.
Obviously.
Obviously.
Obviously.
Obviously.
Thank god you're not my sister.
That's some deadly sibling rivalry.
Nice family.
I'm glad you're not my sister.
I'm glad you're not my sister.
Hello, Commander. Can I get you something?
Your arrival created a bigger-than-average stir among the diplomats and hangers-on around here.
I could fill you in on some points of interest, if you'd like.
So long, Commander. Have a pleasant day.
You know who I am?
What have you got?
Goodbye.
Commander?
Why not?
No, thanks.
Information, mostly. Would you like to know about some points of interest nearby?
Well, you've found the embassies. Not much going on here.
If you need supplies, you can try the markets one level below. For entertainment, I'd try Flux or Chora's Den.
What's going on around here?
Fill me in.
I should get going.
Well, Flux has gambling and dancing. Certainly more lively than this place.
Chora's Den on the other hand.... Let's just say it's livelier and deadlier, all at the same time.
The Consort. She entertains clients who can afford her services.
Most of the diplomats and ambassadors have visited her at one time or another.
Tell me about Flux and Chora's Den.
What is Sha'ira's?
I should go.
Entertainment
Sha'ira's
I should go.
I should go.
Commander. Here for some information?
There's always something new happening around here.
Across the bridge you'll find the bank, the Emporium, and Sha'ira's. If you haven't heard of her, you soon will.
She's a very powerful woman, but also very respected.
Sure.
Hello again, Commander. Can I help you?
If we're lucky, we'll actually realize usable technology from this study in a few years.
Please let me know if you have any other questions.
This is a long-term study. I wouldn't expect the bodies to be released for a year or longer.
Very few bodies had this new type of weapon damage, and very few were in good enough condition to study.
Beyond that, Commander, we need as many bodies as we can to get a reasonable sample size.
I'm sorry, Commander. The needs of the living outweigh the needs of the dead.
The military has made its choice, and it believes that gaining new technology is worth inconveniencing people like Mr. Bhatia.
Studying Nirali Bhatia's body could save the lives of countless soldiers. I can't release her.
Commander, I-- I don't think threats are necessary.
Even if the body were here on the Citadel, would you really risk going in shooting to get it?
Commander, you of all people should understand how far we must go to protect humanity!
All right, Commander. You win. It was hard enough refusing Mr. Bhatia. I'm not going to risk an incident by refusing you.
Tell Samesh that the body is being shipped back to Earth. I'll go now to see to it myself.
My goodness, you're Commander Shepard!
Your activities made for quite a briefing in the Diplomatic Corps! Is there something I can do to assist you?
Ah, Mr. Bhatia. A good man in an understandably frustrating position. I wish I could help him.
Commander, nothing would make me happier. I'm afraid, though, that it's not quite that simple.
Serviceman Nirali Bhatia died on Eden Prime, as Mr. Bhatia no doubt told you.
Her wounds are inconsistent with any type of weapon damage we've seen before. That is why her body is being held.
We are not holding Nirali Bhatia's body out of discretion. We are, frankly, holding the body for research.
No, Commander. Nirali Bhatia is not dangerous. Her body is, in fact, extremely valuable to the Alliance.
The tests we are conducting may lead to better defenses against geth attacks.
Respectfully, Serviceman Bhatia may save more lives in death than she did in life.
That was just the reaction we were hoping to avoid, Commander.
But if you think it will help, tell Mr. Bhatia the truth. Perhaps he will understand.
Thank you. I appreciate that.
When will this research result in actual new technology?
How long do you think the research is going to take?
You've got to have a lot of bodies. Can't you release one?
Thanks for your help.
I'd like you to reconsider releasing Nirali Bhatia's body.
You've got no legal right to keep the body, and I know you don't want this to go public.
You know who and what I am. If I want Nirali Bhatia, I can get her.
You said you'd been briefed on me. You should know that I don't leave fallen troops behind.
You said you'd been briefed on me. How do you think I feel about people mistreating the dead?
You said you'd been briefed on me. How far do you think I'm willing to go on this?
The marine's name was Nirali Bhatia. If you want to cut her up, you call her by name.
I understand what you're trying to do, but holding the body is wrong.
Not if we lose our humanity in the process! I'm out there fighting to stop crap like this!
You've read my file. You know how far I'm willing to go, and I'm telling you to release the body.
Is this what I'm out there fighting for? A government that steals the bodies of its honored dead?
Soldiers shouldn't have to worry about what their own government is going to do to their bodies.
Yes. A man named Samesh Bhatia is having some trouble claiming his wife's body.
You can cut the red tape for a grieving husband. I want you to release the body of Nirali Bhatia.
I'm here on behalf of Samesh Bhatia for his wife, Nirali.
I don't care how badly the geth mangled the body. It's the husband's right to claim her.
You think that her body might be dangerous or contaminated?
You're studying her injuries to learn more about geth weaponry.
I'll tell Samesh. Next time you cut up a dead soldier, at least tell her husband the truth.
I'll tell Mr. Bhatia about this. It might make it easier for him to understand.
Results of Research
Length of Research
Number of Bodies
Goodbye.
Please help Samesh.
Release the body. Now.
Thanks for the information.
I'm releasing the body.
This isn't right.
Thanks for the information.
Thanks for the information.
Thanks for the information.
Yes, I would.
Yes, I would.
Yes, I would.
She deserves better.
Her. Not it, her.
I do, and you're wrong.
It's not worth it.
Not this far.
At what cost?
You're betraying the dead.
I'm here for Samesh.
Stop stealing corpses.
I hope so.
So she's been mauled.
She's toxic?
You're running tests.
I see your point.
Samesh should hear this.
I'll pass this on.
So they finally did it? I knew one of your kind would make Spectre one day.
Was there something you needed, Commander?
Goodbye, Commander.
I'll be going now.
Goodbye.
No, I just don't trust your kind. Not yet.
You humans are eager to take all the power you can get. And you're being given a lot.
If the Council wants to make humanity their new favorite pet, that's their business. But I don't have to like it.
Good. Then fight for it. But don't expect the rest of us to just sit back and let you take it.
I'm a busy man, Commander. Are we done here?
C-Sec provides necessary police and security services throughout the Citadel.
We're a civilian government agency, though many of our members have had military training.
I've been with C-Sec for thirty years. I've never had to break the law to do my job. Not once.
Spectres walk a slippery slope, Commander. Operate outside the law and it changes you. Look what happened to Saren.
Yeah, right. You expect us to believe none of your officers are corrupt?
You expect us to believe none of your officers are corrupt?
That is not a completely accurate analogy, Executor. You cannot deny that some C-Sec officers are corrupt.
You expect us to believe none of your officers are corrupt?
Don't piss in my ear and tell me it's raining. I've known plenty of dirty C-Sec agents.
There are over two hundred thousand C-Sec agents. Some of them are going to be bad. But we don't turn a blind eye to corruption like the Spectres do.
We do our best to find and punish any officer who breaks the law. Spectres -- they'll never come under that kind of scrutiny.
I agree, but they need to be held to a higher standard. They need to be accountable.
Saren's out of control. We both know that. But because he's a Spectre, the Council doesn't want to do anything about it.
They're the right hand of the Council, or so they like to be called.
More like the underhanded side of the Council.
I get the feeling you're not too fond of humans.
The Council treats us like second-class citizens. We have to fight for everything we get.
Tell me about C-Sec.
Sometimes you have to bend the law to keep people safe.
The galaxy needs people like that, people who do the dirty jobs.
What do you know about the Spectres?
Attitude towards humans
C-Sec
Spectres
We're not favorites!
That's a bit naïve.
Spectres are important.
Commander Shepard. I didn't expect to see you here. Did Ambassador Udina send you?
You humans are always so curious. Always sticking your fingers into someone else's pie. Is that the right expression?
Uh, never mind. Forget I asked.
Sorry, Commander. I don't make a habit of giving out details about ongoing investigations.
Have we met before?
I came on my own. I need information.
Nobody sends me anywhere. I just need some information.
Tell me about your investigation into Saren.
Then can you tell me what you know about Garrus?
Who are you?
No.
Does it matter?
I go where I want.
Investigation
Garrus.
Is that the kind of person this galaxy needs?
True. I hope that's something you'll take to heart, Shepard.
True, but the potential is always there.
If the cure is worse than the disease... what's the point?
Maybe. But I've never had to cross that line to get the job done. Never.
Of course, as the C-Sec representative to the Council, I spend most of my time liaising between the two.
I can't abide any organization that considers itself above the law.
Especially when it's left up to each individual Spectre to decide when and how to "bend the rules".
Garrus Vakarian? Good officer. Very good in fact. But he needs to learn some patience.
You'd think an officer of the law would be a bit more mindful of rules and regulations--
Was there anything else?
Shepard. What can I do for you now?
I only hope you're better than the one they're sending you after.
Hmm. That's what worries me.
Was there something you wanted?
Why did you come to see me, Shepard? Did Ambassador Udina send you?
No. But I know you well enough. I'm Executor Pallin, head of C-Sec.
It's my job to know when someone like you arrives on the Citadel.
And, unlike the Spectres, we work within the bounds of the law.
I'll do whatever it takes to stop Saren.
I'll do everything I can to stop Saren.
But not all Spectres are like Saren.
Absolutely. The only thing that matters is accomplishing the task.
What do you have against the Spectres?
No.
If it gets the job done.
You don't like them?
Damn right.
I strive to be.
No.
And you're the first human Spectre. Get used to people knowing who you are, at least around here.
This place seems strange. I wish there were more humans around.
You have to be tough with these aliens. They won't respect you otherwise.
It's good to see another human face around here.
If I have to listen to another hanar take twenty minutes to say the simplest thing, I think I'll scream.
Don't believe the rumors. The Consort would never reveal her secrets.
Of course she wouldn't. She'd be tossed out the nearest airlock if she did.
I suppose.
Besides, Nick, the Consort's nothing like the girls back on the colonies. She's.... She's....
You don't have to do it with her. You can just talk to her if you want.
Is that all you did, Jaz? Just talk?
I didn't say that!
Ha! I bet you did, too.
Shut up, Fredricks.
What do you want?
Calm down, Private, this isn't an inspection.
Right, sorry. What can I do for you, Commander?
Thank you. You too.
I, ah, well, she's an asari who works here as... that is, she helps people with... things.
Ha! You never went to see her, did you, Private?
I, uh, no. I never did. I couldn't afford it. It costs half a year's credits just to go in and talk to her.
Sure, she's across the bridge from the embassies.
Thanks, kid. Have fun. Try not to get into too much trouble.
I will. Have fun, that is.
Commander, good to see you again.
This place is amazing... Commander.
Commander.
I think I'll see if I can get stationed here permanently.
Just saying hi. Enjoy yourself, Private.
What can you tell me about the asari Consort?
That's fine, Private. Just tell me where to find her.
Can you at least tell me where I can find her?
Nothing.
Consort?
I understand.
Where is she?
Commander. What can I do for you?
Oh, Commander.
Relax, Private, this isn't an inspection.
Ha! You've never been, have you, boy?
You never went to see her, did you?
Did you really go to see the Consort?
You never went to see her, did you, Fredricks?
Is there something I can do for you?
